title: The Map with More Than One Center
title_ja: 中心が一つではない地図
fact_notes: 登場人物・学校・具体的な出来事は架空の教材例であり実在の調査や統計ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: During an online international exchange, students from three fictional schools were asked to prepare short presentations about the places where they lived.
sentences.ja: オンライン国際交流で架空の3校の生徒は住んでいる場所について短い発表を準備するよう求められた。

sentences.en: Each group began by showing a map that included its own community and several neighboring countries or regions.
sentences.ja: 各グループは自分たちの地域と周辺国・地域をいくつか含む地図を示した。

sentences.en: One student noticed that the maps looked different even though all of them were intended to represent the same planet.
sentences.ja: ある生徒はすべて同じ地球を表す目的の地図でも見え方が異なることに気づいた。

sentences.en: Some groups had chosen maps with their own region near the center, while other parts of the world appeared close to the edges.
sentences.ja: 自分たちの地域が中央近くにあり、世界の他の部分が端近くに見える地図を選んだグループもあった。

sentences.en: The students began discussing why a familiar map could appear unfamiliar to someone who had learned geography in another part of the world.
sentences.ja: 身近な地図でも別の地域で地理を学んだ人には見慣れないものに見える理由を話し合った。

sentences.en: Their teachers explained that a flat map represents a curved surface and that mapmakers also make choices about which area to place at the center.
sentences.ja: 教師たちは平面地図が曲面を表していること、作成者がどの地域を中心に置くかも選ぶことを説明した。

sentences.en: The class considered how the position of a region on a page might affect the way a viewer initially understands its relationship to other regions.
sentences.ja: 紙面上の地域の位置が他地域との関係についての最初の理解にどう影響し得るか考えた。

sentences.en: They avoided concluding that any particular group had deliberately selected a map in order to make its own country appear more important.
sentences.ja: 特定のグループが自国を重要に見せるため意図的に地図を選んだと結論づけることは避けた。

sentences.en: For their next exchange, the groups agreed to compare two or more representations of the same journey between their schools.
sentences.ja: 次の交流では学校間の同じ移動経路の表現を二つ以上比較することにした。

sentences.en: They prepared diagrams using different centers and examined which countries or bodies of water appeared close to the intended route in each version.
sentences.ja: 中心の異なる図を用意し、それぞれでどの国や水域が予定経路に近く見えるか調べた。

sentences.en: Several students discovered that a journey that looked unusually long on one map appeared quite different when the world was represented from another viewpoint.
sentences.ja: ある地図で異常に長く見えた移動が別の視点から世界を表すとかなり違って見えることを発見した。

sentences.en: They therefore checked geographical distances using suitable reference materials rather than judging travel distance from the appearance of a single map.
sentences.ja: そこで一枚の地図の見た目から距離を判断せず、適切な資料で地理的距離を確認した。

sentences.en: The teachers then invited each group to introduce a place that rarely appeared in the other students' school materials.
sentences.ja: 教師たちは他の生徒の教材にめったに登場しない場所を各グループに紹介するよう求めた。

sentences.en: Instead of presenting their countries as collections of famous tourist destinations, the students described ordinary neighborhoods, local transport, and everyday activities.
sentences.ja: 有名観光地の集まりとして自国を紹介せず、普通の地域、交通、日常活動を説明した。

sentences.en: They also asked questions about how people in the partner communities understood the places they had introduced.
sentences.ja: 交流先の人々が紹介した場所をどう理解しているのか質問もした。

sentences.en: The exchange helped the participants recognize that familiarity with one representation does not amount to complete knowledge of a place.
sentences.ja: 交流を通じ、一つの表現に慣れていることは場所について完全な知識があることと同じではないと認識した。

sentences.en: By the end of the project, the students had become more attentive to the choices involved in presenting geographical and cultural information.
sentences.ja: 活動の終わりには地理的・文化的情報を示す際の選択により注意を払うようになった。

sentences.en: No single map or presentation could include every relevant feature of the world with equal emphasis, and different purposes called for different representations.
sentences.ja: 一つの地図や発表が世界の関連するすべての特徴を同等に強調することはできず、目的によって異なる表現が必要だった。

sentences.en: Comparing viewpoints did not mean abandoning the need to verify factual information; rather, it encouraged the students to examine the assumptions behind familiar images.
sentences.ja: 視点を比較することは事実確認の必要を捨てることではなく、身近な画像の背後にある前提を調べるよう促した。

sentences.en: For the participating schools, the international exchange became an opportunity to learn not only about different places but also about different ways of seeing them.
sentences.ja: 参加校にとって国際交流は異なる場所だけでなく異なる見方についても学ぶ機会となった。

questions.prompt: What did each group show first?
options: A list of international exam scores.
A photograph of every tourist destination.
A map including its own community and nearby regions.
A complete travel budget.
questions.explanation_ja: 自分の地域と周辺地域の地図。

questions.prompt: What difference did the student notice?
options: Maps of the same world had different appearances.
The schools used entirely different planets.
Every map contained identical centers.
No map included any neighboring region.
questions.explanation_ja: 同じ地球でも見え方が異なる。

questions.prompt: What did teachers explain about maps?
options: A world map has only one possible center.
Every flat map preserves all spatial relationships perfectly.
Maps have no relationship to geography.
A flat map represents a curved surface and involves choices about the center.
questions.explanation_ja: 曲面を平面に表すことと中心の選択。

questions.prompt: Why did the class avoid assuming the groups' motives?
options: They had proved that every mapmaker had the same motive.
Different map choices did not establish an intention to promote national importance.
They believed geography had no factual content.
Every student had deliberately chosen a false map.
questions.explanation_ja: 地図の選択だけで動機を確定できない。

questions.prompt: What did groups compare for their next exchange?
options: Different representations of the same journey.
The cost of every international flight.
The number of flags in each classroom.
A list of countries with identical sizes.
questions.explanation_ja: 同じ移動経路の異なる表現。

questions.prompt: Why did they use suitable reference materials?
options: They wanted to abandon every geographical measurement.
The maps had already provided exact travel prices.
A single map's appearance could be insufficient for judging distance.
All journeys had been completed before the exchange.
questions.explanation_ja: 一枚の見た目だけでは距離判断が不十分。

questions.prompt: What did students describe instead of famous tourist sites?
options: Only the longest rivers in the world.
Ordinary neighborhoods, transport, and everyday activities.
The names of all political leaders.
International competitions at their schools.
questions.explanation_ja: 普通の地域や日常活動。

questions.prompt: What did the exchange reveal about familiarity?
options: A familiar image always contains every relevant detail.
No representations offer useful information.
Every place must be visited before it can be discussed.
Knowing one representation is not equivalent to knowing the whole place.
questions.explanation_ja: 一つの表現に慣れることは完全な知識ではない。

questions.prompt: What does emphasis mean in this context?
options: Geographical distance between schools.
A kind of transportation.
Special importance given to something.
A completely hidden detail.
questions.explanation_ja: 特別に重要性を与えること。

options: Comparing representations and verifying facts can deepen understanding of places and perspectives.
All maps other than one's own must be rejected.
Different perspectives make factual verification unnecessary.
Each country can be accurately represented by its tourist sites alone.
questions.explanation_ja: 表現を比較し事実を確認することで場所と視点の理解を深める。

grammar.focus: even though all of them were intended to represent
grammar.explanation_ja: even thoughは強い譲歩、be intended toは目的を示す。

grammar.focus: how the position of a region on a page might affect
grammar.explanation_ja: how節はconsideredの目的語、mightは可能性。

grammar.focus: rather than judging travel distance from the appearance
grammar.explanation_ja: rather thanは選ばない方法との対比。

grammar.focus: did not mean abandoning the need to verify factual information
grammar.explanation_ja: mean＋動名詞は〜することを意味する。

paraphrases.source: One student noticed that the maps looked different even though all of them were intended to represent the same planet.
paraphrases.rewrite: One student saw that maps of the very same planet could look unlike each other.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 同じ地球を示す地図でも見え方が異なる。

paraphrases.source: The class considered how the position of a region on a page might affect the way a viewer initially understands its relationship to other regions.
paraphrases.rewrite: They examined the possible influence of map placement on a viewer's initial geographical understanding.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 地図での配置が最初の理解に与える影響を考えた。

paraphrases.source: They therefore checked geographical distances using suitable reference materials rather than judging travel distance from the appearance of a single map.
paraphrases.rewrite: They consulted appropriate sources for geographical distance instead of relying solely on how a map looked.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 見た目だけでなく資料で距離を確認。

paraphrases.source: Comparing viewpoints did not mean abandoning the need to verify factual information; rather, it encouraged the students to examine the assumptions behind familiar images.
paraphrases.rewrite: Looking at several viewpoints did not remove the need for fact-checking; it helped expose assumptions in familiar images.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 視点の比較は事実確認を不要にしない。

discourse.role_ja: 同じ地球と異なる表現を対比。
見え方の違いから距離確認へ。
典型的な観光紹介から日常紹介へ。
視点比較の目的を正確に示す。
